body_html:
How to think about it

Displacement, velocity and acceleration are vectors. On a displacement–time graph the gradient is velocity; on a velocity–time graph the gradient is acceleration and the area is displacement. For constant acceleration use the equations of motion.

Newton's laws: no net force means constant velocity; F = ma; forces come in equal and opposite pairs. Momentum p = mv is conserved in collisions; impulse FΔt = Δp explains seatbelts and airbags. Work W = Fs; kinetic energy ½mv²; gravitational potential energy mgh.

Example

Car from 0 to 20 m/s in 8.0 s. Acceleration?

a = (20 − 0) ÷ 8.0

Answer: 2.5 m/s²

Example

1200 kg car accelerates at 2.5 m/s². Net force?

F = ma = 1200 × 2.5

Answer: 3000 N

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up distance (scalar) and displacement (vector).
  • Thinking a moving object needs a net force to keep moving.
  • Putting the two forces of a Newton's third law pair on the same object.

faq.q: Why does a seatbelt reduce injury?
faq.a: It stretches a little, increasing the stopping time; for the same change in momentum, a longer time means a smaller force (FΔt = Δp).

faq.q: When can you use the equations of motion?
faq.a: Only when the acceleration is constant, such as free fall without air resistance.

items.q: Why do airbags reduce injuries in a crash?
c: they increase the change in momentum
they increase the time for the person to stop, so the force is smaller

items.q: What is momentum?
What is the difference between distance and displacement?
c: distance has a direction; displacement does not
displacement is the straight-line change in position with a direction; distance is the path length

items.q: What is the weight of a 60 kg student on Earth? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Noah's car goes from 5 m/s to 10 m/s in 10 s. What is its acceleration?
What does Newton's second law state?
c: objects keep moving unless a force acts
the net force equals mass times acceleration, F = ma
items.e: Acceleration is in the direction of the net force.

items.q: What is the work done when a 50 N force moves a box 4.0 m in the direction of the force?
A bike slows from 34 m/s to 10 m/s in 6 s. What is its acceleration?
A runner covers 120 m in 40 s and then 140 m in 20 s. What is the average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 260 ÷ 60 = 4.33 m/s.

items.q: A runner covers 200 m in 25 s and then 70 m in 35 s. What is the average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 270 ÷ 60 = 4.50 m/s.

items.q: A car brakes and a passenger without a seatbelt moves forwards. Why?
c: the passenger's inertia keeps them moving forwards
items.e: Seatbelts provide the force to slow the passenger.

items.q: A car's speedometer reads 60 km/h. What does it show?
items.e: It shows speed at that moment.

items.q: A boy runs round a circular track of length 400 m and comes back to the start in 60 s. What is his average velocity?
items.e: Displacement is zero, so average velocity is 0; average speed is 6.67 m/s.

items.q: Tom's car goes from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
Two balls, one heavy and one light, are dropped together in a vacuum. Which reaches the ground first?
items.e: All bodies fall with the same g when there is no air resistance.

Kai's car goes from 0 m/s to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is its acceleration?
What does the gradient of a velocity–time graph give?
items.e: The area under it gives displacement.

items.q: Which equation has no time in it?
items.e: Use it when t is not given.

What does the gradient of a displacement–time graph give?
A ball is dropped. Ignoring air resistance, what is its acceleration?
items.e: All objects fall with the same acceleration in a vacuum.

items.q: A car speeds up from 12 m/s to 24 m/s over 108 m. Calculate its acceleration.
items.e: v² = u² + 2as, so a = (v² − u²)/(2s) = 2 m/s².

items.q: In which kind of collision is kinetic energy conserved?
c: a collision in which objects stick together
items.e: Momentum is conserved in all collisions.

What is terminal velocity?
c: the speed when an object hits the ground
the constant speed reached when air resistance balances weight

items.q: What does Newton's first law state?
c: every action has an equal and opposite reaction
an object stays at rest or moves at constant velocity unless a net force acts

items.q: A car speeds up from 5 m/s to 8.00 m/s over 39.0 m. Calculate its acceleration.
items.e: v² = u² + 2as, so a = (v² − u²)/(2s) = 0.500 m/s².

items.q: A car speeds up from 5 m/s to 20 m/s over 62.5 m. Calculate its acceleration.

What does Newton's third law state?
c: if A exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A
an object at rest stays at rest
momentum is always lost in collisions
items.e: The pair act on different objects.
